subheading: Extend a photo past its original edges, change its aspect ratio, or undo a bad crop with outpainting workflows in ComfyUI.
extendedDescription:
An image extender adds picture where there was none. You give it a photo and a larger canvas, and the model paints the missing area so the result reads as one continuous scene rather than a photo with a border stuck on. The technique is called outpainting, and it is the fix whenever an image is the right picture at the wrong shape: a portrait that needs to be a banner, a square crop that needs to fill a 9:16 story, or a shot framed too tightly to leave room for a headline.

The featured Expand Image app is the quickest route: upload, choose how much wider or taller you want it, run. Behind it the page carries the full range of outpainting graphs. Outpaint to Any Aspect Ratio and Any Image to Any Aspect Ratio target reformatting directly, so you name the ratio and let the workflow work out what to add. Flux.1 Outpaint, Flux.2 Klein Image Extend, Bria Image Outpainting and Wan2.1 VACE Outpainting give you different models to try when a scene is hard, since results vary a lot with subject matter. Graphic Design Recomposer handles layouts rather than photographs, and Video Outpainting and Video Aspect Ratio Extension apply the same idea to footage.

What the model invents is a guess, so the workflows are editable graphs rather than one button. You control how far to extend, prompt for what should appear in the new area, and rerun the parts that came out wrong instead of starting over. Everything runs on Comfy Cloud in the browser with no install, or locally in ComfyUI, and exports at full resolution with no watermark.

styles.title: Room for copy

styles.title: Video reframing
styles.description: Apply the same extension to footage when a clip needs a different aspect ratio than it was shot in.

howToUse: Start with the Expand Image app for a straightforward extension, or pick an outpainting workflow if you want control over the model.
Open it on Comfy Cloud with the Try button, or load it in your local ComfyUI.
Upload your image and set the target size or aspect ratio.
Describe what should appear in the new area if the workflow takes a prompt, since the model is inventing it.
Run it, then check the seam where the original meets the generated area at full size.
Rerun with a different model or a shorter extension if the new area drifts, then export at full resolution.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between extending and upscaling an image?
faqItems.answer: Extending adds new picture beyond the original edges and changes the framing. Upscaling keeps the same framing and increases resolution. The AI image upscaler page covers upscaling.

faqItems.question: Is the added area real?
faqItems.answer: No. The model generates it based on what surrounds it, so it is a plausible continuation rather than recovered detail. Check the seam and the new area before using the result anywhere it matters.

faqItems.question: How far can I extend an image?
faqItems.answer: Short extensions are reliable; the further you go, the more the model is inventing and the more likely it drifts. Extending in a few smaller steps usually beats one large jump.

faqItems.question: Which workflow should I start with?
faqItems.answer: Start with the featured Expand Image app. If you want a specific aspect ratio, use Outpaint to Any Aspect Ratio, and try the Flux, Bria or Wan graphs when a scene proves difficult.

faqItems.question: Can I extend video too?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Video Outpainting and Video Aspect Ratio Extension apply the same technique to footage, which is useful when a clip has to run in a ratio it was not shot in.

faqItems.question: Do I need to install anything?
faqItems.answer: No. The Try buttons run each workflow on Comfy Cloud in the browser. Local ComfyUI is supported with the same graphs if you prefer your own GPU.
